facts.text: Zug Island was originally a marshy peninsula that served as a Native American burial ground for thousands of years.
In 1859 furniture mogul Samuel Zug bought the 334‑acre parcel at the confluence of the Detroit and Rouge Rivers, hoping to build a family estate.
Zug abandoned the estate after ten years because the dampness proved too much, and the island was sold in 1891 for industrial use.
The island’s name comes from Samuel Zug, one of the founding members of the Republican Party and a noted abolitionist.
A short canal cut through the island in 1888, later enlarged by Henry Ford in the 1920s, allowed large ships to reach the Ford River Rouge Complex.
Today, Zug Island hosts a major steel mill operated by US Steel, whose shutdown in 2020 ended the long‑running “hum” reported by residents.
